soundness_flags.label: ass:low-nuisance
soundness_flags.one_line: The condition q < gamma is not Kennedy et al.'s low-smoothness regime, whose threshold depends on d and the average nuisance smoothness; retag it as a new geometric restriction or replace it with the cited regime.

soundness_flags.label: prop:pair-radius
soundness_flags.one_line: The claimed k=1 sanity reduction uses undefined expectation notation E_s and omits the component law and nuisance sign; state it as an expectation under P_{s,lambda} with k=1.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: honest_scope / oeq:full-fiber-pair-lift
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The full-class pure-private minimax frontier and the uniform score family are not claimed proved; they remain the explicitly stated open-ended lifting problem.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The field-level claim is limited to the exact-uniform signed two-fiber family, its one-record obstruction, the sparse-occupancy pair test, and the finite quantized audit.

source_verification_receipts.version: Annals of Statistics 52(2), 2024, published journal version
source_verification_receipts.locator: Theorem 1 and its low-smoothness discussion, printed pp. 797-799
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The low-smoothness branch is stated using average nuisance smoothness s=(alpha+beta)/2 and the threshold s < (d/4)/(1+d/(2 gamma)); it is not the condition alpha+beta < gamma.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Abstract and publication record; Section 3 in the proceedings paper
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper concerns pure-private testing of two simple hypotheses and a randomized clamped log-likelihood-ratio test.
The paper develops central-DP analogues of Le Cam, Fano, and Assouad using coupling-based lower-bound arguments.
The finite-family T-mechanism guarantee contains log(|P|/beta), and the cover extension contains log(|P_eta|/beta).
The method uses local Hajek projections, data-dependent good/bad classification, and tuple reweighting to control private U-statistic sensitivity.

source_verification_receipts.version: IEEE Transactions on Information Theory 67(3), 2021 version
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Private hypothesis selection over m candidates has logarithmic dependence on m and its infinite-class extension is cover based.
The paper gives a sample-splitting meta-algorithm for private CATE learners, formulated through f-DP with approximate DP as a special case, rather than a pointwise Holder minimax frontier.
Finite CATE queries use Gaussian vector perturbation under (epsilon,delta)-DP, while functional RKHS queries use Gaussian-process perturbation under approximate DP.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Replace the misnamed q < gamma assumption with Kennedy et al.'s actual low-smoothness inequality if that is the intended comparator regime; otherwise retag and justify q < gamma as a new two-scale geometric condition, then restate precisely which regimes the pair-radius result covers.

Resolve the full-fiber lifting question for a nontrivial Hölder subclass, yielding an explicit one-sensitive score family and a full-class pure-DP upper risk theorem rather than only a signed finite-family test.

Add a matching private lower bound or a direct strict rate comparison against a named generic private U-statistic/selection method on the same CATE class, so the pair radius becomes a demonstrated frontier advance rather than a diagnostic-family result.

recommended_next_step: Revise the low-smoothness assumption and the k=1 reduction notation, preserve the accepted finite-family scope, then advance the corrected field-level pair-test core to Stage 0.
